content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm currently experimenting with [product_name] [version_no] for collecting data from several machines. I'm unsure how to set up a connection between [product_name] and [version_no] devices. With some older machines, I'm able to read analog signals and digital inputs/outputs for logging. However, some machines don't allow configuring analog outputs compatible with [product_name] inputs. Is it possible to establish a link between [version_no] (without Profinet) and [product_name]? How can I access the data on [product_name]?

[product_name] [article_no] supports Ethernet TCP/IP with S7 protocol and, starting from [version_no], Modbus TCP/IP. For communication with a [version_no] device, you need a PN CPU or a compatible module that supports PN.

analysis.insight_summary: Users aim to connect [product_name] for data logging with [version_no] units lacking Profinet. The discussion highlights uncertainty over compatible communication protocols and hardware, especially where analog signals cannot be used. Limitations revolve around the specific versions supporting Ethernet TCP/IP and Modbus TCP/IP.
analysis.user_expectations: Users hope for straightforward digital communication between [product_name] and [version_no] for data logging. Guidance on required protocols and compatible hardware is expected.
